title: Generics mind map
intro: Generics let you write reusable code that stays type-safe at compile time and keeps real type information at run time. This module covers why they replaced ArrayList, how to declare and constrain type parameters, variance on interfaces, and a production Result<T> pattern for cache boundaries.

conceptCards.title: Why generics exist
conceptCards.summary: ArrayList stored object with boxing and risky casts. List<T> gives compile-time safety and no boxing for value types.
conceptCards.example: List<int> rejects list.Add("oops"); ArrayList only fails at run time.

conceptCards.title: Types, methods, and inference
conceptCards.summary: Open generic typeof(List<>) versus closed List<string>. Static fields per closed type. Generic sharing: reference T args share JIT code.
conceptCards.example: RedisCache<SessionDto> closes T; typeof(IHandler<>) for DI

conceptCards.title: Constraints on type parameters
conceptCards.summary: where T : IComparable<T> unlocks CompareTo. struct, new(), notnull, and allows ref struct each have exclusion rules.
conceptCards.example: T Create<T>() where T : new() => new T();

conceptCards.title: Covariance and contravariance
conceptCards.summary: out T = producer (IEnumerable). in T = consumer (Action). List<T> is invariant. Value types do not convert.
conceptCards.example: IEnumerable<string> to IEnumerable<object> is legal; IList<string> to IList<object> is not.

conceptCards.title: Result wrapper for APIs
conceptCards.summary: CacheResult<T> separates Hit, Miss, and Fault. TryGet is enough when you only need hit/miss.
conceptCards.example: Redis miss is not null — it is CacheResult<SessionDto>.Miss().
